prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create one collectible naturalist field-journal illustration for the crafting game Éclat, Le Carnet du Semeur. Subject: 'Le Cercle de Pierres', a secluded ancient circle of irregular weathered standing stones in a small grassy clearing within a temperate forest, seen from high above as if observed from a kite. Near-overhead aerial view, subtle perspective just enough to read the stones' height and soft shadows. An imperfect ring of modest rough gray stone monoliths with lichen, open grass in its middle, ferns and a few bushes around the clearing; just a small suggestion of surrounding trees along two irregular edges, avoid a huge forest filling the frame. The ring is the clear central focal point and reads at 150 px wide. Mood contemplative, quiet, archaeological rather than magical. Medium: fine human sepia ink and dry graphite contours, granular muted watercolor in olive, straw ochre, stone gray and warm earth, matching a hand-illustrated botanical travel journal. Light from upper left. Slightly wider than tall vignette with irregular broken brush edges fading to genuine transparency, no hard rectangular edges. No paper background, no frame, no words, no numerals, no diagram labels, no map grid, no glowing symbols, no runes, no people, no kite in view, no fantasy portal, no giant Stonehenge trilithons, no modern objects. This is a close study of the clearing collected in the margin of a notebook, not an entire landscape.
